newsitem.title: USA: US sen asks Rubin to delay muni utilities rules.
newsitem.headline: US sen asks Rubin to delay muni utilities rules.

text.p: A key U.S. senator urged the U.S. Treasury Dept. not to issue tax-exempt bond rules that he said would allow publicly-owned utilities to compete against privately-owned entities.

"New Internal Revenue Service regulations giving publicly-owned utilities a special competitive advantage by authorizing them to use tax-exempt bonds to compete against privately-owned utilities would be inappropriate and contentious," Sen. Frank Murkowski, R-Alaska, said in a July 8 letter to Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin.
"Accordingly, I urge you to withhold from such action," said Murkowski, chairman of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee.

"In my opinion, this is a matter for the Congress to decide, not the IRS," Murkowski said. He added that he is "disappointed" that the Treasury chief did not respond to an April 22 letter on the same issue.
Murkowski noted that tax-exempt bonds that are being used for "legitimate purposes" should not be jeopardized.

"In this regard, I urge you to act quickly to issue private letter rulings in specific cases, such as California, where private use concerns may frustrate turning existing transmission assets over to independent system operators pursuant to a State restructuring plan," Murkowski said.

Murkowski noted that he and Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth, R-Del. believe hearings are needed on how to ensure a "level playing field" as the electric power industry moves toward deregulation.
He said he asked Congress' Joint Committee on Taxation to prepare a report explaining the provisions of the tax code affecting electric power, including tax-exempt municipal financing.
